# The appointments Asanga made — and who is keeping them

The mistake is reading myths as entertainment. Asanga's cycle reads more like a charter — each story assigning a duty the modern world still pays for.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Asanga
- **Pantheon:** Buddhist
- **Domain of influence:** Yogacara, Mind-Only
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Culture & Entertainment
- **Strongest seat:** Education, Research & Knowledge
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 55 of 546

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Education, Research & Knowledge — through *Two Brothers, One Teaching*

Asanga and his younger half-brother Vasubandhu — arguably the two most consequential Buddhist philosophers after Nāgārjuna — were born, the story runs (Xuanzang preserves it in his Great Tang Records of the Western Regions), to a brahmin of Kauśika lineage; their mother, the legend adds, resolved that one son should master the Mahāyāna and the other its rival, the analytical Abhidharma of Kaśmīr.  Vasubandhu became the encyclopedist of the Abhidharmakośa; Asanga wandered and meditated until he founded Yogācāra.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Primary seat: Asanga embodies yogacara, mind-only — the core of education.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Mythic Name Restoration — through *Twelve Years, a Wounded Dog, and Maitreya*

The founding vision of Yogācāra is a story about compassion first.  Asanga, the tradition says (Xuanzang; the Tibetan historians Bu ston and Tāranātha repeat it), spent twelve years in solitary retreat awaiting a vision of the future Buddha Maitreya — and saw nothing.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Resonant seat: Asanga shares symbolic territory with mythic restoration.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Writing, Publishing & Media — through *Yogācāra, the Practice of Mind-Only*

What Asanga built — with Vasubandhu and their lineage — the tradition called Yogācāra, "practice of yoga," and its opponents called cittamātra, "mind-only. " Its masterworks, the Mahāyāna-saṃgraha ("Compendium of the Mahāyāna") and the Abhidharmasamuccaya, set out a psychology of awakening: the store-consciousness (ālayavijñāna), a deep repository in which the seeds of deeds and habits sleep, waiting to sprout as the world; the three natures — the imagined (the snake), the dependent (the rope), the perfected (the seeing); and the radical claim that the "external world" is a construction of consciousness, no more independent than a dream is independent of the dreamer.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Resonant seat: Asanga shares symbolic territory with publishing media.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Asanga's mythology is the hagiography of a psychologist: the vision that founded his school came through compassion for a dog, and his school's charter texts were, by tradition, dictated by the future Buddha — scholarship's verdict is that Asanga wrote them himself, which changes nothing about the parable.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

Skeptical? Good — the system is built for you. Every seat in this file carries its why-line and its weight, the full derivation is public at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/), and the challenge process is part of the design. Falsifiable is not a posture here; it is the mechanism.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in education, research & knowledge, mythic name restoration, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/asanga/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
